Q781.L1t: Alice in Wonderland is a famous children's story in which the heroine meets many odd creatures and experiences strange changes in size.
Q781.L2t: In this part of the story Alice goes into the Rabbit's house, finds a fan and gloves, and notices a bottle by the looking-glass.
Q781.L3t: Alice's head touched the ceiling before she had finished half of the bottle, and she kept growing as she drank.
Q781.L4t: Alice grew huge because she drank what was in the bottle.
Q781.L2f: The Rabbit's house in the story is a big, untidy building with a stone floor and no furniture in the room Alice enters.
Q781.L3f: The Rabbit had planned the whole thing, and Alice's growing started the moment she saw the Rabbit looking scared of her.
Q781.L4f: Alice grew so big because she wanted to frighten the Rabbit.

Q366.L1t: The passage deals with memory, attention and how people's mental abilities change as they get older.
Q366.L2t: Lumosity is a web-based brain training program designed by experts from Stanford University and based in San Francisco.
Q366.L3t: The passage says the brain needs exercise in much the same way as our muscles do, and that the right mental workouts can improve basic cognitive functions.
Q366.L4t: The passage shows that the brain, like the body, needs exercise to stay sharp.
Q366.L2f: Lumosity was built by a company in London as a game for children and has no connection with any university.
Q366.L3f: The passage says Lumosity was tested in one study where students using it did worse on math tests than classmates who did not, and its users reported no real benefit.
Q366.L4f: Lumosity is unreasonable, and the passage shows it is a poor idea.

Q336.L1t: The passage compares several ways to study a foreign language, each with its own strengths and weaknesses.
Q336.L2t: The passage says there are online courses available for a lot of languages, and some of them give support from teachers by email, chat or phone.
Q336.L3t: The passage says some online courses are free but there are some you have to pay for, and that there are plenty to choose from for many languages.
Q336.L4t: Online courses can be taken easily over the Internet.
Q336.L2f: Online courses are described in the passage as available for only a few languages, and all of them need a trip abroad to finish.
Q336.L3f: The passage says that every online language course is offered at no cost, and that only the ones taught in a classroom ask students to pay.
Q336.L4f: All online courses are free of charge.
